items.title: Elvis Presley rightsholders sue Anthropic over alleged training on 274 songs
items.summary: A subsidiary of Authentic Brands Group, with other Presley rights owners, sued Anthropic on Oct 23 in the US District Court for the Northern District of California. The complaint alleges Claude was trained on 274 songs without a licence and can still produce infringing derivative versions when asked to update songs for a modern audience. Reports put statutory damages at up to $150,000 per song. Counsel is Richard Busch, who won the Marvin Gaye estate's 'Blurred Lines' case. Anthropic had not commented in the coverage seen.
items.why_it_matters: It is another music-copyright suit against Anthropic, on top of the publishers' case, and it lands as the company heads toward an IPO where litigation exposure must be disclosed.

items.title: Musk says SpaceX closed $40B of debt for GPUs, predicts neocloud shakeout
items.summary: On Oct 25 Elon Musk posted on X that SpaceX had closed $40B of debt to buy GPUs, mostly callable debt for chips arriving in Q1 and Q2, and 'not a major factor this quarter'. He credited SpaceX's investment-grade status and Starlink and launch revenue. He also said debt markets have nearly shut off financing for firms without substantial revenue outside AI data centres, and that more than 200 neoclouds face consolidation. Earlier reports described an Apollo-led package of bank loans and investment-grade debt tied to an Nvidia chip purchase.
items.why_it_matters: Capital for GPU purchases is concentrating in large rated borrowers while neocloud credit tightens, a theme running through this month's neocloud selloff.

items.title: Moonshot says Kimi K3.1 Pro had cyber-offense data removed in training; internal exploit benchmark falls from 90.5% to 81.0%
items.original_title: 中国最强开源模型杀到！Kimi K3.1 Pro剥离网络攻击数据：编程仍反超GPT-6
items.summary: Moonshot AI says Kimi K3.1 Pro, a post-training upgrade of K3, had cyber-offense and defense data identified and removed during mid-training and reinforcement learning. Chinese media report an internal benchmark, xdev-bench-hard, scoring 90.5% for the unfiltered variant versus 81.0% for the released model. The company reportedly says it will not open-weight a model at the absolute cyber frontier, and full weights are due by Nov 4. Reports also cite a 1M-token context and Terminal-Bench 4.0 at 65.7%.
items.why_it_matters: It is a rare public case of a Chinese open-weight lab describing data filtering to cap offensive cyber capability.

items.title: Nvidia's Huang floats about $2,000 per GPU per year for agent-running software
items.summary: At GTC Berlin on Oct 22, Jensen Huang pegged the cost of Nvidia software that 'runs agents on AI factories' at about $2,000 per GPU per year; Tom's Hardware, Notebookcheck and TechPowerUp wrote it up on Oct 25. It appears to be an illustrative figure rather than a final price. Nvidia has not said which products it would cover or when it would start, and it already sells AI Enterprise at a higher per-GPU price.
items.why_it_matters: It signals Nvidia pushing toward recurring software revenue on top of hardware.

items.title: Shanghai holds first 'AI+Consumption' innovation contest with nearly 800 projects
items.original_title: 上海举办首届“人工智能+消费”创新大赛
items.summary: Shanghai held the awards ceremony of its first 'AI+Consumption' innovation contest on Oct 25 at Xuhui West Bund, organised by the Shanghai Modern Service Industry Federation and West Bund Development Group. About 800 valid projects entered across three 'AI new consumption' tracks and one 'AI new force' track. A 'Qwen AI glasses' retail project won a first prize, as did an AI eye-analysis device.
items.why_it_matters: A local signal of the push to bring Chinese AI hardware such as smart glasses into retail.

items.title: Infinigence AI and Three-Body Universe launch 'Zhizi Agent 1.0', a Three-Body character agent
items.original_title: 国产AI底座赋能国产原创IP智能化升级，无问芯穹与三体宇宙联合发布智子Agent 1.0
items.summary: At the '2026 Three-Body Day' event in Beijing on Oct 25, Infinigence AI and Three-Body Universe announced a strategic partnership and a first product, Zhizi Agent 1.0, a dialogue agent modelled on the Three-Body character Zhizi with cross-session memory and a multi-agent set-up separating persona, knowledge retrieval and content verification. It runs on Infinigence's AgentWorks platform. The company claims its inference architecture cuts time-to-first-token by 51.5% and per-token cost by 37.5%.
items.why_it_matters: A niche but concrete example of a Chinese AI-infrastructure startup tying its agent stack to an IP owner's consumer product.
